name: Leg seam painting

card.summary: Drawing a line up the back of the bare leg to mimic a stocking seam, giving the look of sheer stockings.

quick.overview:
During the Second World War nylon went to the military, so stockings were scarce. A drawn or painted seam on the back of the leg imitated the look of seamed stockings.

The payoff is the appearance of sheer, polished legs without stockings.
quick.how: Leg makeup is applied to the skin and a line is drawn up the back of the leg.
quick.risks: No documented risks beyond ordinary cosmetics.

lead: Leg seam painting is the practice of drawing a line up the back of the leg to imitate a stocking seam. It arose as an imitation of stockings when they were hard to get.
DuPont introduced nylon in 1939, and nylon production was redirected to military use on 11 February 1942, ending civilian stockings; surviving prewar pairs were sold on the black market.[1][2]

angle.text: The line creates the visual impression of seamed stockings on bare legs.

paras: Sheer flesh-coloured stockings began in the 1920s and nylon ones after 1940; DuPont stopped nylon stocking production on entering the war, creating a black market, and postwar demand led to nylon riots.[1][2]
